outbreak_frequency: Kasese outbreak began 2008 (ref Neil 2012), continued through 2011; "epidemics of waterborne/foodborne diseases, such as cholera and typhoid fever, have historically plagued both districts"; no pre-2011 Bundibugyo outbreak noted
endemicity: Not stated as endemic pre-outbreak; authors note "intense, sustained typhoid transmission occurs in rural areas of sub-Saharan Africa" based on estimated annual incidence (409/100k Kasese, 820/100k Bundibugyo) exceeding Kenyan urban slum rates (247/100k)
notes: Outbreak spread Kasese->Bundibugyo via shared water source (Kirumya-Bubukwanga GFS); driver = absence of sustained water intervention after 2009; MDR rose 5%->83%; TCV recommended as medium-term measure pending water infrastructure
